description: Synthetic records of one fictional person's photo library (Maya Fenwick) with fictional relatives and friends, for reproducible acceptance; not a benchmark task. Workflow shapes were informed by Google Photos Help (https://support.google.com/photos/) for shared albums, link sharing, storage and trash, and by the Immich documentation (https://docs.immich.app/) for albums, stacks, shared links and trash; no data, text, photos, branding or icons were taken from them.

sources.description: Story records written out by hand in scripts/build-reference-fixture.cjs: the November 2026 reunion and the other dated photos, the shared albums with their members and contributions, the links and views, the removal requests and their messages. People, places and captions are fictional; no external collection.

The rest of the library generated by scripts/build-reference-fixture.cjs from a fixed seed: outings with capture times from January 2024 to October 2026, screenshots and downloads, stacks and exact duplicates, sizes, the trash and the private albums.

The account history from its opening on 2025-01-04 to the fixture clock, generated by scripts/reference-history.cjs from its own fixed seed: arrival times, edits, items trashed and restored, photos purged, 2025 links, members, views, saves and removal requests, the time each item entered each album, every notification and the activity log.
Stand-in PNG images drawn by dev/draw-images.cjs: flat scenes of colour fields and shapes with light grain and a stamped caption. No people, faces, photographs or generative model.

parameters.seed_from: FNV-1a hash of the item ID

transformations: Timestamps carry explicit UTC offsets; local days are resolved in America/Los_Angeles.

fixtures/reference.json, the images in assets/ and contribution/assets.catalog.json are written by scripts/build-reference-fixture.cjs (with scripts/reference-history.cjs); `--check` confirms they match byte for byte. fixtures/minimal.json is written by hand.

review.notes: Automated checks do not replace human review of realism (library size and metadata, notification wording), of whether the script-drawn stand-in images are adequate, and of the fictional status of every person and place.
